items.title: Nothing's upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
items.excerpt: Nothing confirmed its Dec 8 AI device is the Ear (note): earbuds that record and transcribe audio with AI, capturing from the buds or from microphones built into the charging case. New fact beyond the 11-21 date tease: official product name and type.

items.title: Your next screwdriver might have a camera and an AI brain
items.excerpt: Arrowmax's Arrowspace S1 uses a camera to identify a screw, light up the right bit, and set a safer torque. Kickstarter pricing starts around $79, with shipping in April 2027.

items.title: ASUS Zenbook S14 (UX5406AA) Review: The elegant travel partner I’d pick again in a heartbeat
items.excerpt: Review of the Intel-based ASUS Zenbook S14 (UX5406AA) with a 50-TOPS NPU: a gorgeous 120Hz OLED and all-day battery, but the reviewer says the NPU 'hasn't transformed the way I work'.

items.title: I really wanted the Asus ProArt P14 to be my favorite RTX Spark laptop — and it’s painfully close
items.excerpt: Tom's Guide reviews the Asus ProArt P14, an Nvidia RTX Spark 'portable AI studio' laptop: dazzling 3K OLED and 12.5-hour battery, but the slim chassis forces throttled wattage that runs hot under local-AI and creative loads.

items.title: Lenovo Pro 9n review: 18-core RTX Spark in a fancy chassis
items.excerpt: Tom's Hardware reviews the Lenovo Pro 9n, an 18-core Nvidia RTX Spark AI laptop: elegant OLED workstation with many ports, but expensive, and RTX Spark still needs Windows features to justify its price.

items.title: Copilot+ PCs: Why the NPU is no longer a reason to buy a laptop
items.excerpt: Many holiday laptop deals still carry the Copilot+ PC label, but the NPU barely sets devices apart anymore. items.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy 'pervert glasses'
items.excerpt: The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning they compromise bystanders' privacy, get information wrong and can create unsafe situations for wearers. Regulator action on AI smart glasses.
